findings.english: the texts of the Vaisheshika [note: a non-Buddhist school of Indian philosophy]
findings.why: In this Vinaya commentary the source for the two origins of the view (reasoning and absorption) is the Abhidharma Vibhāṣā tradition, not the non-Buddhist Vaiśeṣika; the note compounds the error.

findings.english: The master should walk, circling to the right of the student.
findings.why: slob dpon slob ma'i gyas su bskor reads most naturally as master and disciple both moving clockwise (to the right) while striking the lines, not the master circling around the student.

findings.english: allow the materials to float
findings.why: What floats in the half-filled copper vessel is the gold or silver pot holding the substances (previous side), not the loose materials.

findings.english: even when being "not without a self" is reversed
findings.why: The Tibetan says that even when selflessness is excluded, the positive entity (the self) is not thereby established; the English makes the excluded term 'not without a self', i.e. the opposite.

findings.english: they should remain simply by looking at the food
findings.why: zan la bltas pa tsam gyis is idiomatic: they are to stay with only food as their due (receiving meals but no share of gains), not literally 'looking at the food'.

findings.english: (ngit) a marker indicating a specific class of verbal endings
findings.why: ṅit designates a root bearing the indicatory ṅ (which takes ātmanepada endings), not a marker of a class of endings.

findings.english: If one perceives them as profound without conceptualizing them
findings.why: med na negates both: if one has no perception of them as profound and does not conceptualize, one practises; the parallel passage on 'unfathomable' confirms this.

fix.find: If one perceives them as profound without conceptualizing them
fix.replace: If one has no perception of them as profound and does not conceptualize them

findings.english: because the blue color [note: original: "sngon", often used as a standard example for sensory perception] has already appeared. When the nature of the blue itself appears, other aspects are precisely what are not clear.
findings.why: སྔོན here is 'earlier/before' (it appeared previously; when it appears in its earlier nature the other aspect is unclear), not 'blue' (སྔོན་པོ).

fix.find: because the blue color [note: original: "sngon", often used as a standard example for sensory perception] has already appeared. When the nature of the blue itself appears, other aspects are precisely what are not clear.
fix.replace: because it already appeared earlier. When it appears in its earlier nature, the other aspect is precisely what is not clear.

findings.english: even if the counter-argument — that desire does not occur in those free from it — is not observed
findings.why: mi mthun pa'i phyogs is the dissimilar case (vipakṣa): even though the reason is not seen to occur in the dissimilar case, the passionless, the sign is still inconclusive.

fix.find: even if the counter-argument — that desire does not occur in those free from it — is not observed
fix.replace: even though the reason is not observed to occur in the dissimilar case (vipakṣa), namely those free from desire

findings.english: [note: the Old Translation period]
findings.why: snga 'gyur here means the earlier translation of this lexicon (and the Indic exemplar), not the Nyingma 'Old Translation period'.

findings.english: The phrase regarding the explanation of the activities means that the results will now be shown.
findings.why: ལས here is the ablative of the root-text lemma 'from these [mahāmudrās] it is explained', not 'activities' (karma).

findings.english: It is not through (mudras) symbolic hand gestures or physical postures
findings.why: In this polemic against consort practice (cf. ཕྱག་རྒྱ་སྦྱོར་བ on the previous side) ཕྱག་རྒྱ is the (karma)mudrā partner, not hand gestures.

findings.english: when the substance remains, its cessation or its new arising would be stated as being the substance
findings.why: The Tibetan says that since the substance persists there is no cessation or arising, so how could these be said to be it; the 'there is none' is lost.

findings.english: Through what karma, Venerable One?
findings.why: The king's question ends 'by what deed does he go about on a golden elephant?', which the English drops, losing the point of the story told next (the wooden elephant).

fix.replace: Through what karma, Venerable One, does he go about on a golden elephant?

findings.english: Therefore, it is said: "Because it is not something to be treated with reverence."
findings.why: "Therefore" (དེས་ན) is the lemma being glossed and the clause is the commentator's gloss; the English makes the gloss into the quoted root text.

findings.english: the six types of relief
findings.why: dbugs dbyung here is ucchvāsa, 'chapter/section': the ritual condenses the six chapters (of the Māyājāla material), not 'six types of relief'.

findings.english: unless they look into the mirror of karma and such
findings.why: The Śakras themselves ascertain, by looking into the mirror of karma, whether the same one or another is reborn, unknown to others; it is not an exception for the ordinary gods.

findings.english: The term "furthermore" indicates
findings.why: The lemma is phyir from the root text's de'i phyir, 'for the sake of that' (i.e. preparatory acts done for the robe), not 'furthermore'.

fix.replace: The term "for the sake of [it]" indicates

findings.english: as if harvesting the blue petals of a lotus
findings.why: The blue utpala petal describes the drawn sword (dark as a blue lotus petal), not the cutting of the hair.

findings.english: this shows his primary qualities
findings.why: The Tibetan says this teaches the non-principal (secondary) sense, not the primary one.

fix.replace: this teaches the secondary sense [of the word]

findings.english: One is desired to be liberated.
findings.why: The verse says that because the mind is freed, he (the teacher) holds these to be liberations (vimokṣa), not that someone is desired to be liberated.

findings.english: Through gestures, all defining characteristics are perfectly completed.
findings.why: In this list of offerings ཕྱག is homage/prostration (followed by joined palms), not hand gestures in general.

findings.english: It should be understood as "The practitioner spoke in this way."
findings.why: The honorific gsungs and the following gloss of the mantra-collection (sngags bsdus pa) show the clause is about the (Blessed One) speaking such a mantra-collection, not the practitioner speaking.

findings.english: To this, he says: "in that very context."
findings.why: The lemma de nyid du (tattvataḥ) means 'in reality', which is the point of the Buddhist reply (in reality the pervader is not apprehended), not 'in that very context'.

findings.english: If those who claim there is no conceptualization in perception argue that conceptualization is something else entirely and thus causes an interruption
findings.why: The objection is put by the opponent against the proponent of non-conceptual perception: 'for one who holds perception non-conceptual, conceptualization is something else, so it interrupts'; the proponents themselves do not argue this.

findings.english: the status of something as a cause is observed through direct perception
findings.why: The Tibetan says that the causality of the posited quality for cloth etc., apart from their well-known causes, is NOT ascertained either by perception and non-perception or (as with the eye) from the cessation of the effect; the English presents the causality as observed and drops 'apart from the well-known causes'.

findings.english:
Are adorned with the precious wheel, the lotus,
The sword, and the eight pillars.
findings.why: Wheel, jewel, lotus and sword are the emblems marking the eight pillars (the eight liberations), so the list is mis-segmented, with the jewel merged into 'precious wheel' and the pillars made a fourth item.

findings.english: the Buddha-Eye will become like that of the Great Vajra Holder
findings.why: sangs rgyas spyan is likely the goddess Buddhalocanā (alongside Māmakī), and the text says she/one becomes like Vajradhara, not 'like that of'.

findings.english: the clarity or lack of clarity of the mind
findings.why: dang ba here is faith/serene confidence (prasāda), as the resumed root line dang ba'i yid kyis dngos grub thob shows; 'clarity of mind' misses the sense.

findings.english: this reality never becomes an object of perception
findings.why: de refers to the saṃbhogakāya under discussion (seen only by those on the bhūmis), not to 'reality'.
